observations.body: The Levites are separated and given for sanctuary service in place of Israel’s firstborn, with the substitution again tied to the day Egypt’s firstborn were struck.
observations.label: Levitical service again recalls the firstborn night

observations.body: The passage presents Service and atonement as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Service and atonement

observations.body: The passage places Firstborn night recalled beside Service and atonement.
observations.label: Firstborn night recalled

payload.posture: Read Numbers 8:14–19 as one movement in Passover, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states the Levites are separated and given for sanctuary service in place of Israel’s firstborn, with the substitution again tied to the day Egypt’s firstborn were struck. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Passover.
payload.title: Levitical service again recalls the firstborn night
